newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Summary list of Sweden's April 15 budget proposal.
newsitem.headline: Summary list of Sweden's April 15 budget proposal.

text.p: Following is a list of items included in the Swedish Social Democratic government's April 15 supplementary budget proposal.
KEY CONTENTS

- A 16.3 billion crown five-point programme of labour market and growth measures in 1998, which will be increased to 21 billion crowns in 1999 and 23.3 billion in 2000. This year, spending on the programme will amount to 5.5 billion crowns.

- Municipalities to get 4.0 billion crowns of the total to boost spending on health care and schools. Another four billion crowns will be made available in 1998 and in years thereafter municipalities will get eight billion crowns annually.
- Increased spending to be financed by a projected budget surplus of 13.9 billion crowns in 1998, up from a previous forecast of from a 10 billion crown surplus.

- The budgetary expenditure ceiling for 1997, 1998 and 1999 are to be retained at 723 million crowns, 720 million crowns and 735 million crowns, respectively, and the 2000 ceiling has been set at 744 billion crowns.
- Demand for local government finances postponed to 2000.
FORECASTS
- Gross Domestic Product (GDP) expected to rise 2.3 percent in 1997 and 2.5 percent in 1998, after rising 1.1 percent 1996.
- Consumer prices seen rising 1.8 percent in 1997, 1.5 percent 1998, 2.0 percent 1999 and 2.0 percent 2000 after falling 0.2 percent in 1996.

- Budget deficit seen at 2.1 percent of GDP in 1997, but in 1998 the government expects to meet its target of balanced books despite increased spending and in 1999 the government expects to achieve a surplus. It aims to have a surplus of 0.5 percent in 1999, 1.5 percent in 2000 and 2.0 percent in 2001.

- Unemployment forecast at 4.5 percent in 2000, down from an expected 7.9 percent in 1997. It is seen at 7.1 percent in 1998, 5.6 percent in 1999. The government had promised to halve unemployment to 4.0 percent by the year 2000.
EDUCATION
- Education will get an extra 500 million crowns in 1997 and the annual sum will increase gradually to reach six billion crowns in 2000.
- 15,000 new university places in 1998 to boost number of students and another 15,000 every year to the year 2000. Places for 60,000 new students will have been created by 2000.
- A new modern apprenticeship training is to be introduced.
- Experimental activities with qualified vocational education will be expanded by 1,500 places the autumn of 1997 and 4,300 the following autumn.
- Adult education to get another 10,000 new places this annually from 1997 to 2000 and will, together with previous decisions be expanded successively to 140,000 places by 2000.
GROWTH, ENERGY, INFRASTRUCTURE MEASURES
- A total of 1.5 billion crowns will be allocated to boost growth in 1998 and the sum will reach 5.9 billion crowns in 2000.
- Policy is to be focused on sustainable growth with 5.4 billion crowns being invested in local investment programmes over three years.

- Nine billion crowns will be invested in adapting the energy system up to the year 2004. The government has previously reached an agreement with the Centre and Left parties to start phasing out nuclear power by closing one of two reactors at the Barseback plant on the southern tip of Sweden.

- A total of 3.3 billion crowns will be allocated to infrastructural investments, including the planned railway Botniabanan along part of the country's east coast as well as infra-structure projects in the cities of Gothenburg and Stockholm.
MEASURES FOR SMALL COMPANIES
- Small companies to get 1.6 billion crowns next year, 1.8 billion crowns in 1999 and 1.7 billion in 1999.
- Further relaxation of owner taxation by letting a larger part of the yield on shares in unlisted limited companies be exempted from tax liability on the part of the shareholder.

- Small companies to be given support. Currently small companies pay five percent less in fees on staff with total wages of less than 600,000 crowns and the government will propose to raise this to between 850,000 crowns.
- The environmental grant for the agricultural sector will be increased to enable full use of European Union subsidies, which will provide an additional 700 million crowns.
- An additional 50 million crowns will be invested in regional business policy.
- Ten million crowns annually will be invested on cooperative entrepreneurship and 10 million on female entrepreneurship.

- The propery tax on hydroelectric power plants, the so called production tax, will be halved to 2.21 percent. Thereby, the level of taxation on electricity production will be at substantially the same level as before the increases in spring 1996. The reduction will be financed by a higher consumption tax.
- High risk protection for employers' costs for sick wages.
- Work on simplifying rules for entrepreneurs is continuing.
LABOUR MARKET CHANGES
- Labour market policies will get 900 million crowns this year, 2.8 billion crowns next year, 1.9 billion crowns in 1999 and 1.6 billion crowns in the year 2000.
- Temporary retirement benefits for people from 63 years of age and for longterm unemployed who are over 60 years old. The regular retirement age is 65.
- Unemployed to be allowed to work in health care, elderly care and child care with 90 percent of a regular salary, paid mostly by the government, for limited period of time.
CHANGES IN BENEFITS
- Costs for state assistance to persons with major functional disabilities is estimated to exceed the budget by 600 million crowns and rules that recently were made stricter will be changed.
- Savings on housing subsidies are to be milder with changes costing 175 million crowns a year.
-- Birgitta Forsberg, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
